incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Multiple NVidia driver resets (Xid/ERR) detected across inference-prod GPU fleet. Affected hosts: gpn-704, gpn-705, gpn-712. Error signature: Xid 13/61 recurring + nv-host-reset entries. Paging oncall now. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-resets — escalate if >3 resets/min or customer impact.
Ronit: I'm on it. Acknowledge page. Logging in to the node consoles and checking pod evictions. Can folks avoid large deploys for the next 30m?
Devon: No infra deploys in the last hour. Saw an uptick in ECC correctable counts on gpn-704 over the last 3h, then the first NV-host-reset at 12:03 UTC. Sending kernel/syslog snippet in a sec.
Devon: syslog excerpt:```kernel: NVRM: Xid (0001:00): 61, PID 0, GPU 0: 00000000:01:00.0```
Sam: Copy — I'm cordoning gpn-704 and gpn-705 now to stop new pods. Will start drains. :white_check_mark:
Sam: Running: ```kubectl cordon gpn-704 && kubectl drain gpn-704 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60```
Ronit: Good. Marie please surface any customer-visible errors to CS and open a temporary bridge for impacted accounts. We may need to route traffic off the affected AZ.
Marie: Creating bridge and posting to customers channel. Noticing increased 502s and retry bursts on inference API: spike at 12:05 UTC. Sample request ids: r-8a3f2, r-8a3f9. I'm adding Aisha to the bridge.
Aisha: On it — I pinged two customers (redacted) and they're seeing elevated error rates and some slow responses. They've queued retries. I'll collect request IDs and sample logs.
Devon: Telemetry note: driver version 540.80 on these hosts. There's a recent microcode push last week but no kernel change. Suggest holding on kernel upgrades; consider driver rollback to last-known-good (e.g., 535.54) if resets continue.
Ronit: Noted. Let's try evacuation first. Sam, after drain, can you place the nodes into maintenance and kick a soft power-cycle of the GPU (nv-host-reset) via the management plane? Avoid full host reprovision until we have data.
Sam: Drain completed for gpn-704. Evac in progress for gpn-705 and gpn-712. Starting managed nv-host-reset command: ```/usr/local/bin/gpu-reset --node gpn-704 --type soft```
Sam: Also observed an OOM kill for inference-container on gpn-712 just before the reset. Log snippet:```oom_reaper: reaped process 45672 (inference) total-vm:3584000kB, anon-rss:3400000kB``` Could be model KV growth + retry storms.
Devon: If KV cache growth is contributing, we should temporarily disable aggressive KV prefetching for the biggest models on those hosts. I can push a config toggle to runtime: `kv.cache.prefetch=false` for the affected pool.
Ronit: Do that, Devon. Sam — once nodes are drained, gate them out of the autoscaler so they don't rejoin automatically (we're seeing flapping). Command: ```cloudctl node update gpn-704 --autoscale-enabled=false```
incident-bot: Update: resets observed lowered from 9/min to 2/min after drains and soft-resets. Continuing to monitor.
Marie: CS updated customers on the bridge. They've asked for ETA on full recovery and whether fallback to dedicated-backup pool is possible.
Ronit: We can route critical traffic to `dedicated-backup` — switching routing rule now. Patch config:```routes.inference.prod.priority: failover -> dedicated-backup``` Applying in 2m.
Devon: I'm taking a snapshot of GPU telemetry (ecc/correctable/uncorrectable, temp, power) and pushing to the incident bucket: s3://infra-telemetry/incidents/2768454321/telemetry.tar.gz. Planning a hardware health scan overnight; may recommend RMA for gpn-712 if uncorrectable ECC is seen.
Sam: After the drains and the routing change, error rates dropped ~70% and retry storms reduced. But we still have one host with intermittent Xid 61. I'll collect dmesg + nvidia-smi -q and attach to the postmortem.
Aisha: Customers acknowledged the fallback and are stabilizing. One asked for rerun of failed requests; we'll coordinate retries once nodes are healthy.
Ronit: OK. Action items: Sam collect logs + OOM traces (assigned), Devon prepare driver-rollback plan and hardware scan (assigned), Marie/Aisha maintain customer comms and provide impact summary, I'll draft initial incident timeline and keep the bridge open for 2h.
Devon: Quick mitigation note — if we do a driver rollback, plan to do it in a canary zone first and monitor resets for 30m before rolling. We'll also keep the nodes cordoned until we have driver+firmware alignment.
Sam: Posting commands used and where artifacts are:```kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpn-712 -o wide > /tmp/pods_gpn712.txt
journalctl -u kubelet -o short-iso > /tmp/kubelet_journal.txt
nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,UTIL,RESET > /tmp/gpu_q.txt``` Artifacts uploaded to the incident bucket.
incident-bot: Next update scheduled in 10 minutes or on major state change.
Ronit: Thanks team. Keep the bridge until Devon and Sam confirm no resets for 60m. We'll convert this to a postmortem if root cause leans to hardware/driver. :white_check_mark:
Devon: Noted. Will start canary driver rollback playbook if we see >1 reset in the next 30m.
Sam: Collected logs and started an overnight node soak test on spare hosts replicating workload to reproduce memory pattern. Adding notes to the incident doc.
Marie: I'll draft customer impact summary (error counts, time windows, affected accounts) and share shortly.
Aisha: Sharing customer replies as they come in. One asks for SLA credit if there is confirmed data loss — flagging for CS leadership.
Ronit: Good catch — include that in the postmortem action items. Closing interim coordination for now, will reopen on any regression. :lock:
